look_here_first: LOOK HERE FIRST · Small UNARMED black-nightshade herb with alternate ovate leaves, tiny white 5-lobed flowers and SHORT yellow anthers. The truly decisive field comparison is with MATURE fruit: S. emulans has GREEN CALYX LOBES APPRESSED/SPREADING against berry base and a fruiting PEDICEL that commonly drops with the berry; S. americanum has strongly REFLEXED calyx lobes and its fruit pedicel generally remains on plant. Photo 2 shows only an IMMATURE GREEN berry—do not overidentify from that.

key_traits.label: Family pattern
key_traits.text: Solanaceae: fused 5-lobed corolla, five anthers, berry fruit; this unarmed black-nightshade complex has simple alternate leaves, unlike prickly buffalobur.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Unarmed green annual or short-lived perennial; simple alternate ovate leaves, entire to shallowly toothed or wavy.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Tiny white five-lobed rotate/star corollas, usually small unbranched flower clusters.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Yellow short anthers typically ~1.0–1.5 mm in FNA, with relatively LONGER free filaments ~0.6–1.0 mm than S. americanum.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Mature berries globose, ca. 5–10 mm, dull or only slightly glossy purplish-black; immature berries green are NOT diagnostic.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Fruiting calyx has small lobes APPRESSED or SPREADING against berry rather than strongly curling back.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Fruit-bearing pedicels often reflexed/recurved, thickened at the apex; the mature berry normally falls WITH its stalk.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Often 6–9 sclerotic granules (hard stone cells) within berry; specialist character requiring safe specimen handling, NOT tasting.

key_traits.label: Habit
key_traits.text: Small unarmed green branching herb common in disturbed places. Absence of prickles alone rules out buffalobur but not similar Morelloid black nightshades.

key_traits.label: Leaf
key_traits.text: Simple alternate ovate to elliptic blades, edges entire, wavy or shallowly toothed. Leaf undersides may be purple tinged but color is variable and not reliable alone.

key_traits.label: Flower
key_traits.text: Small white five-part star corollas, five little yellow anthers (~1.0–1.5 mm according to Flora of North America) with free filaments about 0.6–1.0 mm. Visible anther and filament measurements need macro scale; non-diagnostic wilted flower photos only show shape and placement.

key_traits.label: Fruit
key_traits.text: Dark purple-black, commonly dull or only slightly glossy when ripe, globose, ~5–10 mm. GREEN lobes of fruiting calyx remain APPRESSED/SPREADING, not strongly reflexed. Fruit stalk often reflexed/curved and may fall WITH mature berry; pedicel apex thickens.

key_traits.label: Habitat
key_traits.text: Moist woods, stream banks, gardens, roadsides and disturbed areas. Texas reported by Flora of North America, but Hays county range/occurrence has NOT been audited.

key_traits.label: Management
key_traits.text: Treat as a field ID subject only; do not recommend eating leaves or fruits based on photographs because black-nightshade confusion and glycoalkaloids present risk.

lookalikes.differences: Never split S. emulans and S. americanum from black berry or small white flower alone; inspect short anthers/filaments + mature calyx orientation + fruiting pedicels.
